claims.claim: Platform-aware launcher selection returns agym.cmd for Windows and agym for non-Windows execution, and command_for() uses that selected launcher as argv[0] while preserving all existing provider-neutral arguments unchanged.

A deterministic Windows-only real subprocess regression creates a temporary .cmd launcher and proves Python starts it successfully with shell=False, demonstrating the exact process-launch mechanism required by the production adapter without using external MiniMax credentials or network access.

Native adapter invocation still passes the exact command tuple to the injected runner, preserves cwd/capture/text/check/watchdog semantics, and missing-launcher failure remains fail-closed with no second invocation.

Existing TASK-091 adapter behavior for PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, REPAIR, agym.result.v1 parsing, State Guard, structural output, workspace/HEAD binding, timeout, and no fallback remains unchanged and all focused regressions pass.
Production mutation is confined to the adapter and its focused test file; no worker, proxy, credential, roadmap, Runtime, Dispatcher, Operator, Reviewer, or Publisher behavior is changed.
